correctness.rationale: The exact 20-vertex graph and nonflag face predicate are defined. Two enumerators agree on all 1,048,575 nonempty subsets, producing 53,670 faces. The deterministic 26,823-pair matching leaves a single 0-cell and 23 critical 7-cells; a complete directed check of 335,460 covering relations has no cycle. Discrete Morse theory yields the integral 23-sphere wedge. For all lengths, invariant faces correspond exactly to independent sets of the quotient cycle; orientation signs and the augmented Hopf trace formula yield reduced Lefschetz number minus the cycle independence polynomial at -1. The length-ten value and rational +1/-1 eigenspace ranks then follow without a claim of integral equivariant splitting.

originality.rationale: Full accessible primary material was compared on exact graph complexes and theorem implications. Available theorems cover forbidden paths on paths/cycles/forests, several other higher-independence graph families, and ordinary independence/perfect-matching complexes of Mobius ladders. The closest indexed symmetry results use different complexes; an earlier M14 result does not cover M20 or the infinite trace formula. No covering statement was identified, although publication priority cannot be certified and summary-only adjacent records remain a risk.
residual_risks: Semantic and exact-phrase searches are not exhaustive novelty proofs; an unindexed prior higher-independence representation result could exist.
Two adjacent indexed homology-character records were only materially available as titles/summaries; possible unexpected subsidiary statements remain unchecked.
The twenty-vertex homotopy proof is a finite exhaustive combinatorial certificate and depends on executing the included verifier correctly; the all-length formula has a separate symbolic proof.
No independent mathematical audit or independent publication-priority determination has been performed.

value.rationale: A 23-dimensional high-degree integral homotopy calculation on the highly symmetric 20-vertex Mobius ladder identifies a natural nonflag higher-independence benchmark; the all-length antipodal Lefschetz formula gives a six-periodic, graph-theoretic constraint on rational homology representations. The nontrivial (11,12) eigenspace split is invisible in the Betti number and distinguishes it from ordinary-independence and matching-complex symmetry calculations. The result supplies motivated structural information beyond a routine isolated face count.
